questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Minimum Value Given a Canonical Form on the Unit Sphere
questions.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
2{x}_{1}^{2}\ge -3{x}_{1}^{2},\,-{x}_{3}^{2}\ge -3{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -3{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-3(1)=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -3.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-3.$ But before we conclude that $-3$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-3.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-3(1)^{2}-(0)^{2} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-3.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Quadratic Form on the Unit Sphere
questions.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 8-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +36) & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,7,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=4.
$$

questions.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-4{x}_{2}^{2}\le 2{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result,  

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \le 2{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})=2(1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 2.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $2.$ But before we conclude that $2$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=2.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2(1)^{2}-4(0)^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $2.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Quadratic Form on the Unit Sphere
questions.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -3) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(\lambda -3)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =3,\,2,\,-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=3.
$$

questions.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
6{x}_{2}^{2}\ge 3{x}_{2}^{2},\,4{x}_{3}^{2}\ge 3{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge 3{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=3(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge 3.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $3.$ But before we conclude that $3$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=3.$

Notice that when  $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3(1)^{2}+6(0)^{2}+4(0)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $3.$
